public_rationale: The February 16, 2022 survey identifies continuing obstacles to handling distribution shifts in graph data, including differences in graph structure, tasks and shift types [e1]. The February 21, 2022 experiments find that fine-tuning can worsen accuracy under distribution shift across ten tested datasets, while a two-stage training method improves those results [e2]. These findings support the observation, as of May 31, 2022, that unfamiliar inputs remained a substantial unresolved problem: they document obstacles and useful remedies without establishing a broadly reliable solution [e1; e2].
limitations: The absence of a broadly validated solution is an inference from the inspected public research record, not proof that every possible solution was absent.
The graph survey and selected distribution-shift datasets do not cover every application or kind of outlier.
The evidence does not establish that outlier problems are inherently unsolvable or validate every surrounding criticism of deep learning.

evidence.explanation: The survey identifies unresolved obstacles involving graph structure, differing tasks, and different kinds of distribution shift. It also describes progress, supporting the distinction between useful remedies and a general solution.

Experiments across ten distribution-shift datasets show that improving ordinary accuracy can reduce accuracy after a shift. The proposed two-stage training method improves results, but the paper does not establish a general solution to unexpected inputs.
This earlier survey covers anomaly, novelty, open-set, outlier, and out-of-distribution detection. It supplies background on the breadth of the problem and the existence of many partial approaches.
